description: Polaris monitor pass health, probe latency by transport, queue depth, process health, plus the 8 bottleneck-spotting metric families (DB pool, capacity, pg-boss age, discovery, sample writes, HTTP, jobs).

panels.description: p50 / p95 / p99 wall-clock of one runMonitorPass call. Watch this rise toward the configured cadence as a saturation signal — when p99 approaches your monitor.intervalSeconds, the pool is falling behind.
panels.title: Monitor pass duration (p50 / p95 / p99)

panels.description: Items queued at the start of each pass, by cadence. Sustained non-zero values mean the pool is producing slower than the publisher.
panels.title: Queue depth by cadence

panels.description: Per-cadence work outcomes. crash = unhandled exception in the worker (never expected), failure = the work ran but reported a sad-path result, success = clean run.
panels.title: Work item rate by cadence + outcome

panels.description: p95 probe wall-clock by transport. Compare across fortimanager / fortigate / snmp / winrm / ssh / icmp / activedirectory to spot transport-specific slowness.
panels.title: Probe duration p95 by transport

panels.description: Per-transport probe rate, separated by outcome. Sustained failures on one transport often mean a credential or network issue on a specific integration.
panels.title: Probe rate by transport + outcome

panels.description: Node.js event-loop lag p99. Healthy: under 25 ms. Watch: 25–50 ms. Pressure: 50–100 ms. Saturated: 100 ms+. Polaris tested at 15 ms p99 on a production fleet of roughly 1,800 monitored assets.
panels.title: Event loop lag

panels.description: Node.js process memory: RSS (total resident) and heap used. Watch heap_used trending up between GC cycles for a memory leak.
panels.title: Process memory

panels.description: Node.js process CPU usage (user + system, summed across the event-loop core). Spikes correlate with discovery sync cycles.
panels.title: Process CPU

panels.description: Overall capacity severity from capacityService — drives the Maintenance tab pill and the sidebar critical alert. 0=ok, 1=watch (you have weeks), 2=amber (you have days), 3=red (act now).
panels.title: Capacity severity

panels.description: DB connection pool — current in-use, peak observed since boot, Polaris-owned capacity (Prisma + pg-boss pools), Postgres-side max_connections.
panels.title: DB pool — in use / peak / capacity / max

panels.description: DB pool utilization vs Polaris-owned capacity. peak_observed/polaris_capacity is the actionable line — yellow at 0.7, red at 0.9. When it approaches 1, the app stalls at pool acquisition.
panels.title: DB pool utilization (peak & current vs capacity)

panels.description: Database size now vs projected steady-state at current cadences and retention. Steady-state is what the DB will grow to *if nothing changes* — the gap between the two lines is your remaining growth runway.
panels.title: Database size — current vs steady-state

panels.description: Free-space ratio per filesystem Polaris/Postgres write to. Pre-deduped by stat.dev. Watch threshold at 30%, amber at 20%, red at 10%.
panels.title: Disk free ratio per volume

panels.description: Dead-tuple ratio per sample table. Yellow at 0.2, red at 0.3 — autovacuum is falling behind the insert rate. TimescaleDB hypertables exempt themselves on the capacity reasons side; expect a single non-hypertable line if you've enabled the extension.
panels.title: Dead tuple ratio per table

panels.description: Age of the oldest pg-boss job per queue × state. Pg-boss mode only — stays at 0 in cursor mode. A queue at non-zero depth AND oldest age climbing past ~60s = stalled worker. The watchdog already auto-recovers after 1 min, but the gauge tells you it happened.
panels.title: Pg-boss oldest job age

panels.description: p95 of one bulk write into a sample table. Splits DB-write cost out of the broader monitor work duration so a slow autovacuum / index bloat / lock contention is visible separately from network probe time.
panels.title: Sample-write p95 by table

panels.description: p95 end-to-end discovery wall-clock by integration type, on a 1-hour rolling window (discovery cycles are minutes-long, so a 5m window doesn't have enough samples). 'Is discovery getting slower as we add more devices?' as a graph.
panels.title: Discovery duration p95 by integration type (1h window)

panels.description: Discovery runs by integration type and outcome. Failure rate climbing on one integration usually means preflight credentials / connectivity. Aborted means the operator hit the cancel button (or another discovery superseded a stuck one).
panels.title: Discovery rate by integration + outcome

panels.description: p95 HTTP request duration, top-10 routes by max latency over the window. /metrics + /health are excluded from the source data. Climbing across all routes ≈ DB pool exhausted; climbing on one route = that handler is hanging.
panels.title: HTTP p95 by route (top 10)

panels.description: HTTP requests currently being handled by the Polaris process. Climbing under monitor load = handler backpressure. Combined with DB pool utilization above, this tells you whether the backpressure is in HTTP or DB.
panels.title: HTTP in-flight

panels.description: Request rate by HTTP status class. 5xx > 0 means the application threw an unhandled error (errorHandler caught it); 4xx is mostly auth/CSRF rejects (some background level expected during page navigations).
panels.title: HTTP rate by status class

panels.description: p95 duration of one tick of each scheduled background job. Watch a job's line approach its tick interval (60s for dependencyReconciler, 30s for monitorAssets.heavy, 5s for monitorAssets.probe, 6h for reconcileMapRegions) — that's the early-warning that scheduled work is lagging.
panels.title: Job duration p95 by job

panels.description: Job tick failure rate, by job. Sustained failures on one job = its downstream dependency (DB connection, FMG, an external service) is broken; check the corresponding pino logs by `job` value.
panels.title: Job failure rate
Monitor work duration (by cadence x transport x asset_type)

panels.description: p95 of one monitor work item, sliced by cadence. Top-level signal for 'which cadence is bottlenecked'. Pairs with the per-cadence queue-depth panel above.
panels.title: Work duration p95 by cadence

panels.description: p95 of one monitor work item, sliced by transport. Use this to see whether SNMP, FortiOS REST, WinRM, SSH, or ICMP is the slow leg. Work duration includes DB writes and patch-buffer flushes, not just the network call.
panels.title: Work duration p95 by transport

panels.description: p95 of one monitor work item, sliced by cadence x asset_type. The Capacity Advisor reads the same histogram to recommend worker counts. If a specific cadence/device-class combo dominates p95, that is the slice to scale.
panels.title: Work duration p95 by cadence x asset_type

panels.description: Queued FMG tasks awaiting dispatch on the per-integration single-consumer worker. FMG drops parallel API calls past 1-2 concurrent requests, so every FMG-bound code path funnels through this worker. Sustained non-zero values during discovery are expected; sustained non-zero values OUTSIDE a discovery window indicate a stuck worker.
panels.title: FMG worker queue depth

panels.description: 1 when the FMG worker's PROXY lane (strict concurrency=1) is executing a /sys/proxy/json call; 0 when idle. Persistently 1 across a long window = the proxy lane is saturated, and queue depth above will be non-zero.
panels.title: FMG proxy lane inflight

panels.description: Count of native FMG calls (CMDB, dvmdb, auth - anything that is NOT /sys/proxy/json) currently in flight per integration. Unbounded by design - native endpoints hit FMG's own DB and don't share the proxy concurrency constraint. Persistently high values indicate genuine native-call parallelism (good), not a bottleneck.
panels.title: FMG native lane inflight

panels.description: Pg-boss job counts by queue x state. `created` = queued; `active` = currently processed. Pair with the oldest-job-age panel under Throughput - a queue with sustained non-zero `created` AND oldest age climbing past 60s = stalled worker. Cursor mode: all zero.
panels.title: Pg-boss queue jobs (by queue x state)

panels.description: p95 wall-clock of one rollup INSERT...ON CONFLICT per (tier, table). Hourly tier runs every 30 min; daily runs at 02:30 UTC. Watch for an hourly line approaching 1800s - that is the rollup taking longer than its cadence and starting to fall behind.
panels.title: Sample rollup p95 by tier x table (1h window)

panels.description: Rows currently held in the in-memory write buffer for each monitor sample table. Oscillates between near-0 and the steady-state batch size between 2s flush ticks. A persistently rising value means the flush can't keep up with the enqueue rate.
panels.title: Sample buffer depth by table

panels.description: Patches currently held in the in-memory probe-patch buffer. Oscillates between near-0 and steady-state batch size between 2s flush ticks; a persistently rising value means the bulk UPDATE flush can't keep up.
panels.title: Probe-patch buffer depth

panels.description: p95 wall-clock of one bulk UPDATE flush from the probe-patch buffer. One observation per 2s flush tick. Splits per-flush state-write cost out of monitor-work duration so a slow DB write (lock contention, index bloat) is visible separately from network probe time.
panels.title: Probe-patch write p95

panels.description: p95 wall-clock per phase inside one discovery run. Phase labels match the phaseMark() markers in code (e.g. '1', '2a', '3b', '7.5', '13'). When overall discovery duration is climbing, this panel tells you WHICH phase is dragging - usually a specific FMG API call or DB sweep, not the whole pipeline.

targets.expr: topk(20, histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, integration_type, phase) (rate(polaris_discovery_phase_duration_seconds_bucket[1h]))))

panels.title: Discovery phase p95 (top 20, 1h window)

panels.description: Active monitor queue mode at boot. cursor = in-process light/heavy loops; pgboss = pg-boss queue with per-cadence workers. Set once at startup.
panels.title: Queue mode (cursor vs pgboss)

panels.description: DB connection topology detected at boot. direct = single DATABASE_URL pointed at Postgres; pgbouncer = Polaris app traffic goes through PgBouncer (pg-boss / pg_dump / pg_stat_activity reads via POLARIS_DB_DIRECT_URL).
panels.title: DB connection mode (direct vs pgbouncer)

panels.description: Configured worker count per cadence queue, stamped once at boot. Tune via POLARIS_MONITOR_PROBE_WORKERS / POLARIS_MONITOR_FAST_WORKERS / POLARIS_MONITOR_HEAVY_WORKERS / POLARIS_MONITOR_FLOATING_WORKERS / POLARIS_MONITOR_LLDP_WORKERS / POLARIS_MONITOR_STORAGE_WORKERS.
panels.title: Workers per cadence queue

panels.description: Per-process Polaris connection capacity, labeled by POLARIS_ROLE (web / monitor / discovery / all). In a multi-process deployment, sum across role series for the group's footprint against polaris_db_pool_max.
panels.title: DB pool role capacity

panels.description: Per-tick outcome of the 10-min integrationConnectionTester job, sliced by integration_type and outcome (success | failure | skipped). `skipped` is the in-discovery-run branch (preserves prior lastTestAt/Ok to avoid false-positive failures on healthy FMG). A run of `failure` entries without a `success` follow-up explains why an integration stayed in the Failed state across multiple ticks — pair with `journalctl -t polaris | grep integrationConnectionTester` for the per-tick error message.
panels.title: Integration auto-test rate by type + outcome (1h)

panels.description: Process terminations caused by an unhandled promise rejection or uncaught exception, by role and kind. The counter lives in the dying process's registry, so any single scrape reads 0 or 1 — the operational signal is the RESTART, which is what increase() over a window shows. Steady state is a flat zero. Any non-zero bar means a role died and systemd's Restart=on-failure brought it back: check `journalctl -u polaris-<role> | grep -i 'unhandled promise rejection\|uncaught exception'` for the structured fatal line naming the origin. Repeating bars are a crash loop, which is otherwise invisible outside journald.
panels.title: Process crashes by role + kind (1h)

panels.description: Total process crashes across every role in the last 24h. Should be 0. Anything above 0 warrants reading the fatal log line before it ages out of journald.
panels.title: Process crashes (24h)

panels.description: Boots REFUSED because a different hostname held a fresh (younger than 90s) active-instance heartbeat on the same database — two app instances pointed at one database, which double-polls every device and duplicates every alert. `holder` is the hostname that owned the stamp. Read a bar as the guard working: the second instance was stopped, not admitted. The refusing process exits immediately, so a scrape can miss the increment altogether — a non-zero increase() is definitive, the absence of one is inconclusive, and the durable record is the fatal log line plus the Event. Steady state is a flat zero; a bar means someone pointed a second app host at this database, so find out which and why (see docs/HA.md, and note POLARIS_HA_HEARTBEAT=off disables the guard entirely).
panels.title: Refused boots by heartbeat holder (1h)

panels.description: Total boots refused by the active-instance heartbeat in the last 24h. Should be 0. Anything above 0 means a second app instance tried to come up against this database and was stopped — the guard held, but the topology is wrong until you know which host it was. See docs/HA.md.
panels.title: Refused boots (24h)
